answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate cannot be met through renewal or negotiation with the incumbent (they refused reopening). Memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to the low-cost vendor delivered both sharp unit cost reduction and reliable onboarding/invoicing. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate alone, directly addressing the financial constraint. However, assembly line buffer is thin (94% of committed volume), creating execution risk. Verifying memory_c2's original record will confirm onboarding velocity and invoicing accuracy under time pressure. Memory_c4 shows negotiation recovered margin but does not suggest the incumbent will reconsider after explicit refusal. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock pricing, but we lack 14 days and multi-year budget authority. A standard_experiment scale allows faster implementation than broad_rollout while containing risk through close monitoring of the first 30 days post-switch. If onboarding falters or quality issues surface, we retain the option to invoke add_second_source (memory_c3) for the next cycle. Downstream risk is flagged because single-vendor switch at 94% line utilization creates vulnerability to vendor operational failure, but financial mandate and incumbent inflexibility eliminate safer alternatives within this decision window.
